transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. I'm seeking help because I've been experiencing really extreme mood swings lately. I go from periods of intense energy where I feel incredibly high and irritable, to suddenly crashing into feeling deeply depressed and empty.
During those periods of intense energy, have you ever experienced a time where your behavior was so extreme that it required hospitalization or caused significant legal or financial trouble?

I haven't been hospitalized, but I have run into severe financial trouble during those high-energy periods. I've gone on reckless shopping sprees and made some really rash, poorly planned business investments. It has caused a lot of financial distress for both me and my family.
How long do these high-energy periods typically last before you crash—do they usually continue for at least a week, or do they resolve more quickly?

They last much longer than just a week. In fact, my last high-energy phase went on for about a year and two months before I finally crashed into depression. It was a very long, exhausting stretch of being constantly wound up.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Bipolar I Disorder, Bipolar II Disorder]. The patient reported high-energy periods lasting over a year (far exceeding the 4-day threshold for hypomania and the 1-week threshold for mania) and severe functional impairment (significant financial distress). Given the duration and severity, Bipolar I Disorder is the primary clinical consideration, making Bipolar II Disorder unlikely.
